- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust quickly; apply early correction (day 5–7) to align with sentiment turn.
- For 30d forecasts with high event density (≥20 events), model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast curve by reducing slope magnitude by 10–20%.
- If policy_count > 0, model often underestimates price impact; add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to forecast mean for 30d horizon.
